prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: one game ability VFX token atlas, 1024x1024 square RGBA with a truly transparent background. Exactly FOUR isolated hand-painted fantasy effect emblems in an exact evenly spaced 2 by 2 cell grid. Cell centers at 25% and 75% of image width/height. Keep each emblem entirely within the central 65% of its cell, with transparent gutters and no crossing between cells. No text, labels, frames, circles around icons, UI buttons, background, full characters, numbers, decorative borders, shadows or scenery. These are small rendered effect tokens and HUD icons; actual range shapes are rendered separately by the game. Strong distinct silhouette, detailed painted material, restrained glow, readable at 32px. Avoid large opaque panels. Depict characteristic tools/energy/material symbols, not a screenshot or miniature scene. Cell order: TOP LEFT passive, TOP RIGHT skill1, BOTTOM LEFT skill2, BOTTOM RIGHT ultimate. Original avatar: Maelis Chromabloom. Character visual motifs: older museum conservator, square terracotta paint smock with elaborate ceramic mask repair, enormous collapsible gallery frames; paint is a **structural medium**, not a stream of colored blasts.
TOP LEFT: Surface Memory. Ability concept: when a projectile strikes a Maelis canvas, the canvas stores one imprinted property of that projectile (physical/magic/utility; never copies the ability or exact damage), one property per frame.
TOP RIGHT: Unroll the Canvas. Ability concept: erects a 55-GU-wide 2-HP translucent canvas for 3.5 s. It blocks ordinary projectiles from **both** teams but permits walking through with a 15% brief movement penalty. No invisible walls.
BOTTOM LEFT: Restore the Missing. Ability concept: repaints a damaged canvas, restoring one HP and changing its surface into a **one-way reveal window** for 2 s; projectiles still obey the same obstruction rules. If no frame exists, instead creates a 30-GU reveal brush stroke (lower power).
BOTTOM RIGHT: Private Exhibition. Ability concept: joins up to three frames into an open-sided gallery for 4 s. Frames rotate one after another every 1.1 s, opening new shooting angles while closing others. Each rotation briefly releases a burst based on the stored property (capped damage or shield pulse, not copied spells). Public arrows preview next positions.
